result:
The proposed answer N(N+1)/2 fails the N = 1 case, so I reject it.

For N = 1 the solution is a single algebraic soliton of the massive Thirring model. As I recall, this soliton is regular, with no poles for real or complex x in the relevant sense. The formula N(N+1)/2 gives 1 pole in the upper half-plane at N = 1, which is inconsistent with that.

The proposed solution also asserts that the denominator has degree N(N+1) and that its zeros come in conjugate pairs. It gives no derivation for either claim.

The count I recall from the literature on these double-Wronskian rational solutions is N(N−1)/2 poles in the upper half-plane for large |t|. This gives 0 poles at N = 1, which fits. I am going from memory here and have not derived it.

VERDICT: REJECT
